title: feat(lint): advise a template default that reads like a variable path, and a notify node missing a required template variable
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DXuamRUC67fx2TTYrFfyuSH)_

Fixes #32678

Clause-②: yes (widening) — two advisory rules and their exports are added; nothing that saved, built or validated before is refused.
Metadata-protocol: none

## Maintainer quick read

- **What:** two new authoring-time advisories (warning, never a refusal). A template `default:` argument that reads like a variable name warns that it prints that text literally; a flow `notify` node that sends a declared email template without a variable the template marks required warns that every send fails with `MISSING_VARIABLES`. The guide gains "a default is literal text; to read another variable, compute it in the flow".
- **Why:** ruling 6845318122, letter B: no new template syntax; the existing literal `default` and `required` declarations stay, and only authoring diagnostics are added.
- **Risk / rollback:** warnings only; nothing that saved or built before is refused; zero hits in this repo's templates and examples. Roll back by reverting this PR.
- **Read first:** `packages/lint/src/validate-notify-template-variables.ts` (`mayBeSupplied`), `packages/lint/src/validate-email-template-default-arguments.ts` (`pathShapeOf`), `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts` (two registrations: one on the publish door, one CLI-only).
- **Two-minute check:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run src/validate-email-template-default-arguments.test.ts src/validate-notify-template-variables.test.ts` → 2 files, 29 tests green.

## What changes

Ruling record 6845318122, letter B: no new template syntax. The mail renderer's `default` formatter already prints a literal fallback, and a variable declared `required` already refuses the send with `MISSING_VARIABLES`. Two authoring-time checks are added in `@objectstack/lint`, following `email-template-hole-grammar`:

- **`email-template-default-reads-as-path`** (`validateEmailTemplateDefaultArguments`, `warning`, advisory tier). An unquoted `default` argument that reads like a variable path prints that text: `{{ person_name | default:first_name }}` prints the word `first_name`. "Reads like a path" = an `@`-marked path (the `currency:@path` form), a dotted path, a snake_case name, or a plain name the template itself uses as a variable (a declared `variables` name or another hole's path). A quoted argument is never flagged, and quoting is the way to say the literal is meant. Doors: `os validate`, `os build`, `os lint`, and the runtime publish door for `email_template` writes, where it rides the save response as an advisory and refuses nothing.
- **`notify-template-variable-missing`** (`validateNotifyTemplateVariables`, `warning`, advisory tier). A `notify` node names an email template the stack declares, and its `templateData` provably does not supply a variable a locale member declares `required`. Judged the way the renderer's lookup reads a path (split on `.`, from the root): a CEL value envelope counts as supplied (computed per run, never guessed), as do `appName`, `baseUrl` and the keys of the stack's own `email.defaultTemplateContext`; a literal is walked, and a missing key, a non-object or `null` is missing. A template the stack does not declare (built-in, another package's, Studio-authored) is not judged. Each locale member is judged with its own `variables`. Doors: the three CLI commands only (`RUNTIME_NEEDS_FULL_SNAPSHOT`: a flow write's snapshot does not carry the email templates).
- **Severity of the notify check: `warning`, not `error`.** The render context has a contributor the stack does not always state: a host can hand `EmailServicePlugin` a `defaultTemplateContext` in code, and a variable supplied there is supplied to every send. The family's gating precedent (`validate-notify-email-field-recipients.ts`) gates only on a certainty about literals; this verdict is not one. A refusal would also be a narrowing (a flow that saves today would fail to save), which this check does not need.
- **Docs** (`content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx`): the line "a default is literal text; to read another variable, compute it in the flow", both rules, and a fix to the page's own `notify` example (below). The four CLI transcripts that print the author-time rule count move from 65 to 67 (`check:docs-transcript-drift`).

## Acceptance notes

- **The guide's `notify` example could never deliver.** It passed `templateData: { 'task.title': … }` to `crm.task_done`, which declares `task.title` required. A `templateData` key is one name, not a path: the renderer's lookup reads `task.title` as `title` under `task`, so the send failed with `MISSING_VARIABLES`. Measured against `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts` `requireVars` on this tree: `{ 'task.title': 'Ship' }` answers `MISSING_VARIABLES: task.title`; `{ task: { title: 'Ship' } }` is supplied. The example now passes `task`. The new rule names this case in its hint, and pins it.
- **Skills line owed.** The ruling asks for the same line in skills; `skills/**` is a governed surface and is not touched here. Owed: the line "a default is literal text; to read another variable, compute it in the flow" in the published skill that teaches email templates.
- **Not covered: the in-app template dialect.** A flow's inline `notify` `title`/`message` and other text slots use the in-app dialect, which has the same `default` formatter and the same trap. This PR judges email templates only, the surface the card and the ruling name.
- **Not covered: holes with no `default` that the node does not pass.** The ruling names variables the template requires; a hole the template does not declare `required` still prints empty when absent, and is not judged.
- **Corpus measurement:** no email template, example or fixture in this repository writes an unquoted `default` argument the new rule flags (`git grep` over `*.ts`, `*.yml`, `*.json`, `*.mdx`), and no example flow sends a declared template through `notify`, so neither rule adds a finding to a shipped app here. The pull is HotCRM's six templates and four flows.

## Tests

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (whole package, on 1894f0ad, rules and tests unchanged since): Test Files 210 passed (210), Tests 8894 passed, 5 skipped (8899).
- New files: `validate-email-template-default-arguments.test.ts` (15) and `validate-notify-template-variables.test.ts` (14): 2 files, 29 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck`: exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck` OK; the test layer compiles under `tsconfig.test.json`).
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` email-template door tests against the rebuilt lint (`runtime-authoring-gate.email-template-writes`, `-unknown-formatter`, `-formatter-shape`): 3 files, 8 tests passed.

<details><summary>Ablation (one leg per rule; mutation landed and was restored by blob hash)</summary>

- Leg 1, `validate-email-template-default-arguments.ts`: deleted the snake_case branch of `pathShapeOf` (anchor 1 → 0, blob ef0ab3fa6aac → 1bdfa37657bf). The rule's test file: 6 failed | 9 passed (15). Restored: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Leg 2, `validate-notify-template-variables.ts`: an absent `templateData` root read as supplied (anchor 1 → 0, blob 407744cb590c → c7c5093deeb4). The rule's test file: 9 failed | 5 passed (14). Restored: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- The lint tests import the rule from `src` (relative imports), so no `dist` leg applies.

</details>

## Verification

- 90 commands exit 0, among them `check:nul-bytes`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:doc-anchors`, `check:docs-transcript-drift` (red at 65 before the transcripts were moved to 67, green after), `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:published-files`, lint's `check:doc-formula-expressions` and `check:doc-security-posture`.
- NOT MEASURED: `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`, exit 3: its positive control is pinned to a commit this shallow checkout cannot reach (checker health only, not a PR verdict).
